parole.significato: A wild chile pepper variety, Capsicum annuum var. glabriusculum, found in Mexico and the southwestern US.
parole.testo: From Nahuatl; the first element is chilli (“pepper”), the second is tecpin (“flea”).

parole.significato: An isometric dark green mineral containing copper, hydrogen, lead, oxygen, and tellurium.
parole.testo: From Nahuatl choloa (“evasive”), because it was not found in the type locality mine for several years, + -lite.

parole.significato: A plant used as soap in Aztec culture, probably Cyrtocarpa procera.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Nahuatl copalxocotl.

parole.significato: A monoclinic blood-red mineral with the chemical formula Pb²⁺₂Fe³⁺₃(Te⁴⁺ O₃)₃(SO₄)O₂Cl.
parole.testo: From Nahuatl eztli (“blood”), for the mineral's appearance, + -ite.

parole.significato: A bird of the species Opisthocomus hoazin of the order Opisthocomiformes, with claws on the wing fingers of the juvenil…
parole.testo: From Nahuatl huāctzin (which probably designated a different bird).

parole.significato: The mountain goat (Oreamnos americanus)
parole.testo: From Nahuatl mazameh.

parole.significato: The Mesoamerican belief that certain human beings can transform into animals.
parole.testo: From nahual + -ism. The first element is from Nahuatl nahualli (“sorcerer, spirit, animal form a person may take”).

parole.significato: A member of an ancient pre-Columbian people living in the tropical lowlands of south-central Mexico, in what are roughl…
parole.testo: From Nahuatl, meaning rubber lineage (compare Nahuatl olli (“rubber”)).

parole.significato: A Latin American morning glory (Ipomoea corymbosa, syns. Turbina corymbosa, Rivea corymbosa) whose seeds are hallucinog…
parole.testo: From Nahuatl.

parole.significato: Abies religiosa, the sacred fir, an evergreen coniferous tree of South America with needle-like leaves.
parole.testo: From Nahuatl [Term?].

parole.significato: Any of various indigenous peoples of southeastern Veracruz and Oaxaca.
parole.testo: Nahuatl [Term?]

parole.significato: A piece of standardized cloth used as currency in Mesoamerica until shortly after the arrival of Europeans.
parole.testo: From Nahuatl [Term?].

parole.significato: The tropical fruit from the sapodilla tree, Manilkara zapota. The fruit is 4–8 cm in diameter, has a fuzzy brown skin w…
parole.testo: Latinization of Nahuatl tzapocuahuitl (“Manilkara zapota, sapodilla”)

parole.significato: Any of the South American lizards of the families Teiidae and Gymnophthalmidae.
parole.testo: From teguexin, from Nahuatl tecoixin (“lizard”).

parole.significato: A large South American lizard with yellowish spots; a gold tegu.
parole.testo: From Nahuatl tecoixin (“lizard”); compare tegu.

parole.significato: A scalar field that acts as torsion potential.
parole.testo: From Nahuatl tlapal + -on. Attested from 1978 in physics literature.

parole.significato: An animal companion which accompanies a person from birth to death.
parole.testo: From Nahuatl tōnalli (“day, day sign”).

parole.significato: The hispid pocket gopher (Heterogeomys hispidus).
parole.testo: Native to Mexico, from Nahuatl tuçan, togan.

parole.significato: The earflower, Cymbopetalum penduliflorum, sometimes used by the Aztecs to flavour cocoa.
parole.testo: From Nahuatl xōchinacaztli (“ear-flower”), from xōchitl (“flower”). So called because it somewhat resembles an ear.

parole.significato: A telluride mineral found in cracks in altered rhyolite.
parole.testo: From Nahuatl xocomecatl (“grapevine”) (alluding to its appearance as a set of green spherules), and -ite.
